findings.description: The function does not handle the ZeroDivisionError exception, which will cause the application to crash if b is 0.
The function lacks type hints, making it difficult to determine expected input types and return types.
The function does not handle ZeroDivisionError, which will cause the application to crash if the divisor is zero.

reasons: The candidate code now includes explicit type hints for both input parameters and the return type.
The candidate code explicitly checks for division by zero and raises a ValueError, which prevents the application from crashing due to an unhandled ZeroDivisionError.
All test cases passed, confirming the implementation handles both standard division and the zero-divisor edge case correctly.
